title: rutracker + kinozal .torrent download SKIP — ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED (final): the client enqueues the .torrent to Android SYSTEM DownloadManager, which rejects the goapi's SELF-SIGNED TLS cert (CertPathValidatorException) → HTTP_DATA_ERROR → WAITING_TO_RETRY → never completes. Test-harness cert-trust regression (goapi cert regenerated ~10h ago; emulator system store has no CA). NOT the exit IP, NOT the account, NOT client-1078 code.
class: test-harness TLS-trust regression (self-signed goapi cert not in emulator system trust store) + a latent production limitation for LAN self-signed proxies
status: ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED via logcat + production-code trace. Was truly device-green 2026-07-02 => regression.
SUPERSEDES_EARLIER_CLAIM: An earlier version of this file stated ROOT CAUSE = transient per-exit-IP throttle on the OLD Mullvad exit. That hypothesis was FALSIFIED: the keystone re-run on the HEALTHY exit (141.98.253.210) SKIPped identically, while a direct host-side authenticated download on that same exit delivered a real 187KB .torrent in 0.63s. The host-side test verified the goapi->kinozal layer, which is NOT where the keystone fails — the keystone fails one hop earlier, at client-systemDownloadManager -> goapi TLS. Recorded per §11.4.6 (no standing unconfirmed/false 'CONFIRMED' claim).

confirmed_root_cause.chain: Challenge70 taps Torrent -> client resolves the .torrent download URL (the goapi HTTPS endpoint, self-signed cert, reached via adb reverse 127.0.0.1:8443) + session headers -> core/downloads/impl/DownloadServiceImpl.kt:18 downloadTorrentFile() calls context.getSystemService<DownloadManager>() and enqueues DownloadManager.Request(uri) -> Android SYSTEM DownloadManager (process com.android.providers.downloads) uses the SYSTEM trust store, which does NOT contain the goapi's self-signed CA -> java.security.cert.CertPathValidatorException: Trust anchor for certification path not found -> status HTTP_DATA_ERROR -> WAITING_TO_RETRY -> the DownloadDialog stays 'Downloading file…' and never reaches 'Download completed' -> Challenge70 honest SKIP at 60s.
confirmed_root_cause.logcat_proof: DownloadManager: [15] Stop requested with status HTTP_DATA_ERROR: java.security.cert.CertPathValidatorException: Trust anchor for certification path not found. -> [15] Finished with status WAITING_TO_RETRY (x2, then app cancels at teardown).
confirmed_root_cause.why_gutenberg_passes: HTTP-file downloads (gutenberg/archiveorg) go through DownloadHttpFileUseCase -> HttpDownloadSource (in-app OkHttp, which DOES trust the goapi cert via the app network-security-config) -> DownloadServiceImpl.downloadHttpFile persists bytes. The API doc states this path 'does NOT enqueue a DownloadManager'. Only the .torrent path uses system DownloadManager, so only it hits the system-trust-store cert failure.
confirmed_root_cause.regression_evidence: 2026-07-02 kinozal=PASS(clean,marker true), rutracker 1080p=PASS(clean), rutracker mp3=PASS => the .torrent download COMPLETED then. 2026-07-03 all SKIP with the cert error. UNCONFIRMED trigger hypothesis: the goapi TLS cert was regenerated when its container was rebuilt ~10h ago (./start.sh -> lava-api-go/scripts/gen-cert.sh) for cdb46f9a/b4a0f4bc; the emulator system store trusts no self-signed goapi CA (the QA harness has NO cert-install step — grep of lib-emulator.sh/lib-backend.sh/run-iteration.sh found none).

ruled_out: Exit IP / VPN egress — FALSIFIED (re-run on healthy exit still SKIP; host-side auth download works 0.63s).
Account / credentials — kinozal login succeeds (302->userdetails), host-side authenticated /download.php delivers a real 187KB application/x-bittorrent.
goapi code / goapi->upstream egress — that layer works host-side; the failure is client-side before it (system DownloadManager TLS).
Client-1078 code regression — 1078 changes nothing about download; the same client completed a 24.8MB gutenberg HTTP-file download (in-app path) clean.

two_real_findings.A_test_harness_gap: The autonomous-QA harness never installs the goapi's self-signed CA into the emulator system trust store, so the system-DownloadManager .torrent path can only pass when the emulator happens to already trust the cert. FIX (harness): install the goapi CA into the emulator system store (adb root+remount -> /system/etc/security/cacerts, or API34 APEX cacerts) as a QA setup step, matching a production CA-trusted backend. This is a §6.N.1.2 gate-touching change (needs Bluff-Audit + falsifiability rehearsal). It tests the production-against-trusted-cert path — it does NOT fix finding B.
two_real_findings.B_latent_production_limitation: downloadTorrentFile uses system DownloadManager, which CANNOT be given a custom trust manager. Against a CA-trusted deployed goapi it works; against a SELF-SIGNED LAN-discovered proxy (_lava._tcp mDNS, the local-network-discovery use case) system DownloadManager will reject the cert and .torrent downloads will FAIL for real users — while HTTP-file downloads (in-app OkHttp) succeed. Product decision: route .torrent downloads through the same in-app trusted path as HTTP-file downloads, OR document the LAN-proxy .torrent limitation. RESOLVED 2026-07-03: the .torrent download now routes through the same in-app trusted OkHttp path as HTTP-file downloads AND through the provider-aware /v1/{provider}/download route (the root /download is rutracker-only) — kinozal .torrent keystone device-GREEN (verdict=PASS, Download completed x15).

sixth_h_note: SEPARATE §6.H concern surfaced while reading the logcat: OnboardingViewModel logs the full LoginResult INCLUDING the provider sessionToken (a credential-equivalent cookie) to logcat at Debug level ('cred path: login(kinozal) result=LoginResult(... sessionToken=uid=...; pass=...)'). Session credentials MUST NOT be logged (§6.H/§6.AC). Recorded here; value NOT reproduced. Should be redacted in production logging.
banked_green_this_session: gutenberg (sherlock) device-GREEN (clean PASS, real 24.8MB in-app download, video).
impact_on_redistribute: The .torrent keystones cannot re-confirm green until the harness cert-trust is restored (finding A). The client APK 1078 itself is not the defect. Whether to also address finding B (LAN-proxy .torrent) is an operator product decision.
diagnostic_hygiene: Challenge70 60s->240s diagnostic edit was reverted (verified clean). All creds/session handled without echoing (§6.H); the one logcat value that contained a session token was redacted in every grep.
